widget.prompt: Radius 4. Open the central angle to 90° and read the arc length off the circle.
widget.successFeedback: 90° is a quarter of the full turn, so the arc is a quarter of the circumference: (1/4)(8π) = 2π ≈ 6.28. That is the whole idea behind s = rθ — the arc is just the fraction of a lap the angle sweeps, and radians make that fraction the angle itself.
widget.lowFeedback: Not far enough round — the arc is still shorter than a quarter of the circle.
widget.highFeedback: Too far round — you have opened the angle past 90°.

refusals.title: The Radian; Degrees ↔ Radians, Fluently
refusals.why: RE-CHECKED in S204B after tf-02-03 (refused in the SAME S203Q group) turned out recoverable via circleMeasureExplore's arcSector mode. These two were re-read individually against that engine. arcSector slides a central ANGLE and reads arc length and sector area as fractions of the circumference/area — it genuinely models tf-02-03's arc-length questions. It does NOT model tf-02-01 (what makes one radian exactly that size — a definition question about the radius-to-arc correspondence, with no target quantity to reach) or tf-02-02 (converting 5π/6 to degrees, and a matchPairs of degree/radian equivalents — unit restatement with nothing to slide toward). Refusals stand, now individually checked rather than inherited from the group.
